newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market ignores Dow, eyes election.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market ignores Dow, eyes election.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ignored Friday's rally on Wall Street, with the key Straits Times Industrials Index down by mid-morning on Monday.
One dealer attributed the fall to uncertainty ahead of Singapore's general election, which must be held by April 1997.

"That is an issue. There is a concern as to how much percentage the PAP (People Action Party) will get. It's a matter of confidence reading," a dealer with a local institution said. At the last general election in 1991, the ruling PAP won 77 out of the 81 parliamentary seats.
At 0230 GMT, the STII was down 6.34 points at 2,142.52.
Another dealer said the general slowdown in key sectors like property, electronics and tourism had also dampened interest.
Total market volume was thin at around 20.0 million with gainers leading losers by 117 to 55. The UOB OTC Index, which tracks mostly Malaysian OTCs, edged up 6.55 points to 1,195.48.

Malaysian-linked Magnum Corp led the actives with 1.9 million shares, of which about 107,000 shares were blocked at S$2.35-2.48. Malaysian-linked Technology Resources led the gainers, rising S$0.14 to S$3.84.
Among blue-chips, Singapore Press Foreign and OCBC Foreign both fell, shedding S$0.50 and S$0.30 respectively.
